nodes.label: Database Connection Topology (ADR-0007)
nodes.rationale: The runtime Worker cannot open raw TCP, so it must use Supabase's transaction pooler (port 6543); drizzle-kit's session-level advisory locks break under transaction pooling, so migrations need a direct/session connection (port 5432). Two connection strings, one secret name each; prepare:false required.

nodes.label: Normalized Catalog Lookups (ADR-0009)
nodes.rationale: Lookup tables (print_sizes, attires) plus per-package inclusion rows discriminated by kind, over JSONB or free text, so sizes/attires are queryable and constrained, the CMS can edit inclusions later, and combined attire contexts preserve catalog order.

nodes.label: Booking-Time Price Snapshot
nodes.rationale: The price a customer was quoted must survive later catalog price changes; packagePriceCents and per-add-on priceCents are server-written at booking, and client-supplied prices are never trusted.

nodes.label: Integration Tests Against Real Postgres (ADR-0008)
nodes.rationale: A mocked query builder cannot catch a wrong column name — the class of bug M1 can introduce — so tests run against real Postgres (compose locally, service container in CI) and fail loudly when the db is unreachable.

nodes.label: URL Path Versioning /api/v1 (ADR-0010)
nodes.rationale: Zero frontend consumers is the last free moment to version; URL-prefix only, additive-only within v1, breaking changes ship under /v2, and /health stays top-level.

nodes.label: Re-runnable Catalog Seed (db:seed)
nodes.rationale: The catalog file is the source of truth; a re-runnable seed populates 3 Branches, 11 Service Packages with Inclusions, 6 Print sizes, 7 Attires, 2 Add-on Services, reviewed line-for-line against docs/catalog.md.

nodes.label: Appointment Kind (scheduled | walk_in | visitation)
nodes.rationale: kind records how a session happens without building the deferred walk-in booking and visitation flows; the column only records, the flows stay out of scope.

nodes.label: Uniform Error Shape {error, details?}
nodes.rationale: One error shape for every failure, pulled forward from the M2 pre-flight into M1.4 so two shapes never coexist once the api-client starts Zod-parsing errors.

nodes.label: M2 Pre-flight — Shared API Client Spec
Shared API Client @sevendays/api-client (ADR-0006)
nodes.rationale: Both frontends need the same REST API; without a shared layer each app hand-rolls fetch/base-URL/parsing/error code and the two implementations drift. Hono RPC type inference turns route changes into compile errors instead of runtime bugs.

nodes.label: Hono RPC Type-Sharing (AppType)
nodes.rationale: The client takes the API as a devDependency and imports only its types — erased at runtime, no runtime coupling — so 'routes stay chained' becomes a standing API review rule.

nodes.label: Server-Mediated Frontend→API Topology
nodes.rationale: The browser talks only to its own app; all API calls run from TanStack Start server functions, so auth tokens never reach browser JS, inter-app CORS stops being a concern ahead of the hardening milestone, and API_URL comes from server env with no fallback.

nodes.label: Uniform Error Envelope (apiErrorSchema)
nodes.rationale: Every non-2xx conforms to one error envelope {error, details?} and surfaces as one typed ApiClientError carrying status + parsed details, so client error handling is a single code path.

nodes.label: Typed ApiClientError Class
nodes.rationale: UI code branches on failure kinds without string-matching messages; every API response is Zod-parsed at runtime so unexpected data fails loudly.

nodes.label: One Acquisition/Error Seam (candidate D)
nodes.rationale: Every route re-implements the same five-line acquire-try-catch-500 cross-section; policy held by copy-paste erodes by copy-paste. One middleware + one onError + one notFound move the policy into Hono's structure where it holds by construction.

nodes.label: Db-Free /health Endpoint
nodes.rationale: A database misconfiguration should show as API failures while uptime monitoring still reports the Worker itself as up.

nodes.label: Deferred 405 Handling
nodes.rationale: The framework has no built-in method-mismatch surface; a correct 405 needs per-route method-set knowledge, which belongs beside the M2 pre-flight restructure it exists to serve.

nodes.label: Per-Request DB Client (ADR-0011)
nodes.rationale: The client is created fresh per request, preserved exactly and relocated into one middleware so the acquisition-inside-the-try ruling and the rationale stop being pasted comment copies.

nodes.label: Catalog Row-Shaping Builders (candidate C)
nodes.rationale: Row-shaping knowledge is encoded independently by the seeder, the test fixtures, and the truncate list; pure builders lift entry+lookup→row/junction-pair shaping into one module consumed by all three, so shapes agree by construction.

nodes.label: Schema-Derived Truncate List
nodes.rationale: The hand-named ten-table truncate list mirrors the schema export and drifts the next time a migration adds a table; deriving it from the exported Drizzle schema removes the third copy.

nodes.label: One-Transaction Natural-Key Upsert Seed
nodes.rationale: Upsert-vs-insert is a real behavioral fork; folding the write layers behind one writer would grow a 'how' knob and drag test-harness concerns into the production package — the writers stay separate deliberately.

nodes.label: Deepen the Appointment Intake Module Spec (candidate A)
Transactional Appointment Intake
nodes.rationale: The create write inserts the Appointment then its add-on junction rows with a partial-write window between them; M3's slot capacity check-then-insert is racy unless the path is transactional first. One transaction wraps reference resolution and both inserts, also closing the deactivate-between-read-and-insert TOCTOU.

nodes.label: Module-Owned Rejection Messages
nodes.rationale: Rejection wording is a caller concern today — the module returns a bare reason string and the route owns the reason→message map. Typed failures carrying their user-facing message move that interface complexity into the module so routes stay thin.

nodes.label: Log-Before-500
nodes.rationale: Every route catches and returns the uniform 500 without logging — the exact silence that hid deploy blocker #2 (per-isolate db client) until wrangler tail + temporary instrumentation surfaced it; each thrown error must log server-side before the uniform 500.

nodes.label: Live Transaction-Mode Pooler Probe (Seam 3)
nodes.rationale: Workerd/pooler behavior does not show up in Node-env compose tests — the class of gap that let deploy blocker #2 ship invisible. Under transaction-mode pooling an explicit transaction pins one pooled connection for its duration; supported but unproven until a one-shot rehearsal-style probe passes on the live URL.

nodes.label: Read-Stitch Module groupChildren (candidate B)
nodes.rationale: The Map-group-join parent/children assembly idiom is hand-rolled five times (two call sites + fixtures) with order-preservation and empty-group rules living as comments; one pure function owns assembly. The user ruling overrides waiting for a fifth caller: two call sites and three re-derivations justify the module now.

nodes.label: Append-Only created_at Ordering Proxies
nodes.rationale: Junction tables carry no position column; queries pin order with ORDER BY over append-only created_at, and assembly preserves whatever order the query delivers — a persisted order column stays a future migration watch-item.

nodes.label: API-Local Module Boundary
nodes.rationale: The db package owns schema, client, and migrations; row-assembly for the API's reads is not its concern, and moving it there would widen an interface for consumers that don't exist.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: CI runs the exact gates developers run locally (pnpm check + pnpm build) with Node 24 and a frozen lockfile, so the M1 data-layer work lands already guarded.

nodes.label: Env Examples + .dev.vars Gitignore
nodes.rationale: Committed .env.example/.dev.vars.example document the two connection strings so a fresh clone knows the env contract and the DB password cannot be committed by accident.

nodes.label: Manifest Alignments (lucide-react, @types/node)
nodes.rationale: Version inconsistencies fixed so the next dependency re-resolution cannot silently downgrade or diverge.

nodes.label: Shared Zod Catalog Schemas
nodes.rationale: Every new entity gets a shared Zod schema as the API-boundary contract (print size, attire, inclusion union by kind, add-on service, appointment kind + add-on refs), mirrored in Drizzle; shapes are never redefined per app.

nodes.label: Offline-by-Design Migration Generation
nodes.rationale: db:generate diffs schema files only and never connects, so the ticket is offline by design — no live database, no Supabase, no connection strings; the first migration is generated once after every table exists.

nodes.label: Per-Workspace Vitest Configs (ADR-0003)
nodes.rationale: Every workspace with tests needs its own vitest.config.ts — the shared passWithNoTests setting turns a discovery miss into a silent green.

nodes.label: Re-Runnable Natural-Key Upsert Seed (db:seed)
nodes.rationale: Single-transaction natural-key upsert with per-package inclusion rebuild, anchored by unique natural keys; reruns are idempotent and ids stay stable.

nodes.label: psql-Equivalent Verify-Seed Read-Back (db:verify-seed)
nodes.rationale: psql is not installed on this machine; acceptance read-back is a committed probe that quotes counts and spot rows and compares inclusion signatures line-for-line against docs/catalog.md — never a connection string.

nodes.label: Session-Mode Pooler Refinement
nodes.rationale: The direct IPv6-only host (db.<ref>.supabase.co) is unreachable from this WSL2 machine (ENETUNREACH, 0 IPv4 / 1 IPv6 DNS record); the session-mode pooler at port 5432 preserves drizzle-kit's session-level advisory-lock semantics and is IPv4-reachable.

nodes.label: First-Apply FK Index + Natural Key Ruling
nodes.rationale: Before the first db:migrate ever runs, migration 0000 must carry the 7 FK indexes and 3 unique natural keys; after first apply they would be migration #2, which must not happen — the migrations folder is frozen after apply.

nodes.label: Frames Table + package_inclusions.frame_id
nodes.rationale: Frame identity so a multi-picture frame = N inclusions sharing one frame_id; frames are catalog templates with no appointment linkage, numbered per package (explicit 'Frame 1/2/3' headings or listed order).

nodes.label: package_inclusion_attires Junction
nodes.rationale: Atomic attire rows (Toga, Filipiniana, Executive, Uniform) plus a junction replace the single attire_id column and the combined-name rows; picture inclusions require ≥1 attire (privileges 0..N), and combined contexts render in catalog order, never alphabetized.

nodes.label: ADR-0009 In-Place Revision
nodes.rationale: Owner-sanctioned single in-place revision of ADR-0009 to supersede the combined-form decision and record the frames deferral→decision; deliberately no ADR-0010.

nodes.label: M1.4 Real Routes + Integration Tests Plan
Compose PG17 Integration Test Harness
nodes.rationale: Global setup pings the db (fail loud: 'start the compose db') then programmatically migrates; serial test files, truncate-between-tests, minimal hand-written fixtures — the compose database is never catalog-seeded.

nodes.label: Programmatic migrateDatabase Subpath Export
nodes.rationale: One self-contained migration path for local and CI: the db package exposes migrateDatabase(url, opts) that opens its own postgres-js client, migrates, and closes it.

nodes.label: Active-Row Reference Resolution
nodes.rationale: Service Package and Add-on Service references must resolve to active rows; unresolvable references return 400 with per-entity messages; price snapshots are server-written, client-supplied prices never trusted.

nodes.label: REJECTION_MESSAGES + Message-Carrying Failure
nodes.rationale: The failure variant of CreateAppointmentResult gains message: string; wording moves from the route's reason→message map into the module, byte-identical, and the route's failure branch becomes one badRequest(c, result.message).

nodes.label: probe-pooler-transaction.mjs (Seam 3)
nodes.rationale: One-shot live probe over the transaction-mode pooler (port 6543, refuses non-remote/non-6543 URLs): manual BEGIN/ROLLBACK, sql.begin throwing-callback rollback, and commit legs, printing derived facts only.

nodes.label: Confirmation Gate (compose + live probe)
nodes.rationale: The insert-txn ledger item closes only when BOTH the passing compose suite (Seam 2) and the passing live probe (Seam 3) hold — compose-green alone does not; if the probe fails, the transaction decision reopens per the spec's fallback.

nodes.label: verify-appointment-row.mjs Probe
nodes.rationale: psql is not installed; row confirmation is a committed secret-safe probe (confirm/delete/absent modes, derived facts only) that reads the saved POST response from stdin as expectations — asserting the API wrote exactly what it returned.

nodes.label: Four-Act M1 Exit Gate Runbook
nodes.rationale: Pre-flight audit → create via the deployed API → confirm the row in Postgres → user redeploy + survival + public-list read-back → negative controls on the final deployed artifact → evidence-before-deletion cleanup.

nodes.label: Deployed Negative Controls
nodes.rationale: Unknown servicePackageId and malformed-payload POSTs must return the uniform 400 JSON error shape on the deployed Worker; non-400 or a bare not-found body is a blocking finding that reopens the branch and redeploys.

nodes.label: Extract the Read-Stitch Module Spec (candidate B)
